summary: At 2026-08-28T14:12:00Z consumer lag records spiked to 140,000, processing time rose to 310 ms and partner webhook latency to 305 ms, while the consumption rate dropped to 8 records/sec. Correlation analysis over the 14:00‑14:12 window shows near‑perfect positive correlation between processing time and webhook latency, and strong negative correlations between both of those metrics and the consumption rate.

evidence.interpretation: Consumer lag records peaked far above the baseline mean of 45, indicating a sudden backlog accumulation.
Message processing time increased sharply from a baseline mean of ~0.93 ms, suggesting slower handling of messages.
Partner webhook latency spiked to 305 ms, whereas prior samples were effectively zero, indicating a new delay in external calls.
Consumed records per second fell dramatically from a baseline mean of 1,230, reflecting a sharp reduction in throughput.
Processing time and webhook latency are almost perfectly positively correlated over the window, indicating they move together.
Consumption rate and webhook latency show a strong negative correlation, suggesting higher latency coincides with lower throughput.
Message processing time and consumption rate are strongly negatively correlated, indicating slower processing aligns with reduced record consumption.
